newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Voting begins in Bulgarian presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Voting begins in Bulgarian presidential poll.

text.p: Voting got under way in Bulgaria on Sunday in presidential elections which will offer a crucial mid-term test of the popularity of the ex-communist government.
Polling stations opened at 6 a.m. (0400 GMT) but electoral officials in the capital Sofia said they expected most people to vote later in the day.
Voters facing soaring prices and communist-style shortages over the coming winter look set to rebuff the candidate of the ruling Bulgarian Soocialist Party, Culture Minister Ivan Marazov.
Polls show lawyer Petar Stoyanov, candidate of the Union of Democratic Forces and other opposition parties, ahead of Marazov but short of a first round majority.
Outgoing president Zhelyu Zhelev lost a U.S.-style primary to Stoyanov in June and is not contesting the poll.
The president's duties are largely ceremonial but the vote will measure the electoral mood half way through the term of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's Socialist government.
A total of 13 pairs of presidential and vice presidential candidates are contesting a poll. Polls close at 7 p.m. (1900 GMT) and preliminary results are expected early on Monday.
If no candidate wins more than 50 percent, or if turnout is less than half the 6.75 million registered voters, a second round will be held a week later.
